module_title: Modern Physics, Quantum Theory, and Indian Contributions
introduction: In the 20th century, physics leaped into quantum mechanics, relativity, and solid-state electronics. This level covers these complex theories, essential modern devices, and the brilliant contributions of Indian scientists.

core_concepts.title: Quantum Theory
core_concepts.description:
Discoverer: Max Planck (1900). 
He proposed that energy is not radiated continuously, but rather in small, discrete packets called 'Quanta' (or Photons in the case of light).

core_concepts.title: Theory of Relativity
core_concepts.description:
Discoverer: Albert Einstein (1905). 
He formulated the world's most famous equation, $E=mc^2$, proving that mass and energy are interchangeable forms of the same thing.

core_concepts.title: The Transistor
core_concepts.description:
Inventors: John Bardeen, Walter Brattain, and William Shockley (1947). 
This invention revolutionized the entire world. Every modern computer, smartphone, and electronic device is built upon microscopic transistors.

core_concepts.title: Important Devices and their Full Forms
core_concepts.description:
1. LASER: Invented by Theodore Maiman (1960). Full form: Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. 
2. RADAR: Invented by Robert Watson-Watt. Full form: Radio Detection and Ranging.

important_entities.name: The Raman Effect
important_entities.significance: He discovered the 'Raman Effect' regarding the scattering of light. For this, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930. To commemorate this discovery (made on Feb 28), India celebrates 'National Science Day' every year on February 28th.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Students often assume Einstein won the Nobel Prize for his Theory of Relativity ($E=mc^2$). FALSE! He was awarded the 1921 Nobel Prize for his explanation of the 'Photoelectric Effect'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Robert Watson-Watt invented RADAR, which uses Radio waves for Detection and Ranging (finding distance of aircraft).

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC/State PCS frequently asks: 'Why is National Science Day celebrated on Feb 28th?' Always remember: It marks the discovery of the Raman Effect, NOT C.V. Raman's birthday.
